lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Where are all the good-looking ones, Hermes? The men and the women. Show me around — I'm new here.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: No time, Menippus. But look over there, to the right — Hyacinthus, Narcissus, Nireus, Achilles, Tyro, Helen, Leda, and all the ancient beauties.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: All I see are bones and skulls stripped bare. Mostly the same.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Those are the very bones the poets admire. You seem to despise them.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Show me Helen anyway. I wouldn't be able to tell her apart.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: And for that they launched a thousand ships from all of Greece? So many Greeks and foreigners killed? So many cities destroyed?

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: You never saw her alive, Menippus. Even you would have said it was no wonder to suffer so long for a woman like that. Dried flowers look ugly once the color's gone, but when they're blooming they're at their best.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: What amazes me, Hermes, is that the Greeks didn't realize they were toiling over something so short-lived and quick to fade.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: I haven't got time to philosophize with you, Menippus. Pick a spot wherever you like, lie down, and I'll go fetch the other dead.
